finding: Repairs course timetables made infeasible by unexpected changes. finding: A Kempe change swaps the two colours on a bicoloured connected component. The paper studies the complexity of finding the fewest Kempe changes that transform one given k-colouring into another. It admits a (highly non-trivial) polynomial-time dynamic program on paths. It is NP-hard even on star graphs, yet has a constant-factor approximation and is fixed-parameter tractable in k.

finding: In (k-1)-degenerate graphs all k-colourings are Kempe-equivalent, but the known sequences can be exponentially long. If treewidth is at most k-1, any two k-colourings are equivalent within O(k n^2) Kempe changes. For maximum degree Delta, Delta-colourings are equivalent within O(n^2) Kempe changes, unless Delta = 3 and a component is a 3-prism.
limitations: Pure graph theory. Polynomial bounds on sequence length, not algorithms for minimal repair.
title: Kempe changes in degenerate graphs

finding: Analyses the expected time for randomized search heuristics ((1+1) EA, RLS with a bounded palette minimising conflicts; iterated local search with an unbounded palette and a Kempe-chain mutation operator) to rediscover a proper or high-quality colouring after up to T edges are added. algorithm: (1+1) EA, RLS, iterated local search with Kempe-chain mutation; tailored mutation near inserted edges
title: Time Complexity Analysis of Randomized Search Heuristics for the Dynamic Graph Coloring Problem

finding: For edge-dynamic graphs, proposes ways to turn the feasible colouring at time t into an initial colouring at t+1, for random changes and for changes with probabilistic future information.
